newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-PM CANDIDATE SAYS REFORM PACE TO INCREASE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-PM CANDIDATE SAYS REFORM PACE TO INCREASE.

text.p: The pace of Latvian reforms has to be increased in order to achieve better results in the second half of 1997 and in 1998, prime minister candidate Guntars Krasts said in a Radio Latvia interview on Friday.
"We have to achieve better results in the second part of 1997 and in 1998 and therefore we have to increase the pace of reform," Krasts told in a radio interview.
He said this was a complex task as it had to be combined with providing a social safety-net for those who were failing to benefit from reforms or were lagging behind.
"We have to reach a further growth of the gross domestic product (GDP) and we really have to achieve a balanced budget," Krasts said.
"We will aim to achieve the balanced budget in 1997, and even if we fail, it is a must for 1998, which we will implement," Krasts added.
Krasts said that his government would continue most of the reforms initiated by Shkele's cabinet, including education and health-care change.
Krasts said the coalition parties were unanimous that a different approach was needed in administrative territorial reform and more information needed before it was carried out.
Krasts said four smaller parties joining the big three -- Democratic Party Saimnieks, Latvia's Way and Fatherland & Freedom/LNNK -- would add to government stability.

"Theoretically we could govern the country (without them) as the big factions control more than 50 MPs (in the 100-seat parliament)...but the small parties joining the coalition would add to stability," Krasts said.
Krasts has said that his government line-up would largely match the coalition of outgoing Prime Minister Andris Shkele.
